title: C++ core language
intro: The C++ core-language features of each standard, in the order of cppreference's compiler support pages, with their feature-test macros. Rows without a macro are features that matter to a back end. Rows cover the features the EDG front end implements; features it lacks (for example contracts and expansion statements) are not listed. A macro value is listed when the front end defines that value or a later one; values above the front end's maximum are not listed. Status is for the cpfe-cir front end plus the CIR back end on x86-64 Linux (Itanium ABI).

rows.feature: Virtual functions, covariant returns and thunks
Pointers to data members and member functions
Multiple and nested inheritance, base casts
Empty bases and members, tail-padding reuse (Itanium layout)
Function and class templates, explicit specialization, vague linkage
Member functions, const members, calls through bases
Constructor and destructor order, temporaries, cleanups
rows.note: Order, cleanups and temporaries work. A temporary that a mem-initializer binds to a reference member (lifetime-extended outside an initialization) is diagnosed and the function is dropped. The writer also diagnoses a conditionally lifetime-extended temporary and an array of objects whose destructor is not known; no input in the M6.1a probes reached them.

rows.feature: Static storage duration, dynamic initialization, function-local statics
Static data members and static member functions
new and delete expressions, array cookies, class operator new and delete
new (std::nothrow), the allocation function may return null

rows.note: Members of anonymous unions and structs work. A member whose path through the unnamed member cannot be built (for example an initializer with a destructor in one) is diagnosed and the function is dropped.

rows.feature: Copying an array of class objects (implicit copy of a class with an array member)
rows.note: The copy or move constructor, implicit or defaulted, of a class with an array member (also nested, or in a base or member class) of a class type that has a non-trivial copy constructor is diagnosed ("the copy of an array of class objects in a member initializer"): the constructor is dropped, so a program that uses it fails to compile. An array of trivially copyable elements, and the copy and move assignment operators of such a class, work. The copy of an array by a structured binding or a lambda capture is diagnosed too. Before M6.1a the writer sent the element copy without its source argument and the program crashed or was miscompiled.
The front end folds constant expressions, so the back end sees constants.
Evaluated by the front end; no code is generated.

rows.feature: Strongly typed enums and enum base types
thread_local (block scope, dynamic initialization and destruction)
thread_local (namespace or class scope, dynamic initialization or destruction)
rows.note: The definition is dropped with a named reason; the _ZTW/_ZTH wrappers are not emitted yet. An extern thread_local is accessed directly, not through its _ZTW wrapper, so the dynamic initialization of a variable defined in a g++ object is skipped (pre-existing; planned with the row).
The evidence uses [[gnu::...]] attributes only; no CIR run test uses a standard attribute such as [[noreturn]]. Optimization-only attributes are accepted and ignored.

rows.feature: Return type deduction for normal functions

rows.note: The front end folds constant expressions, so the back end sees constants.

Default member initializers work in constant initializations and when they do not name another member. A default member initializer that uses the implicit this in a non-constant aggregate initialization (a local, a new-expression, a return; designated or positional) is diagnosed ('a reference to a parameter by position') and the function is dropped.

rows.feature: Arrays of runtime bound (the ATS, GNU variable length arrays)
rows.note: This is the GNU variable length array extension (N3639 did not enter C++14). It is diagnosed and the function is dropped; the negative test is a C program that shares the diagnose site.

rows.note: Evidence in --c++11 GNU mode (the test enables the feature as an extension). Copying *this into the closure has the same semantics and code in every mode.

rows.note: Evidence in --c++11 GNU mode (the test enables the feature as an extension). __builtin_launder is a builtin whose mapping does not depend on the mode.

rows.feature: constexpr dynamic allocation (new and delete in constant evaluation)

rows.note: A member skipped by the designators whose default member initializer uses the implicit this, in a non-constant initialization, is diagnosed and the function is dropped (see cxx14.aggregate_nsdmi). Since main's GH #260 a skipped member gets its default member initializer in GNU C++ before C++20.
Scalar destroying delete, also through a virtual destructor, works. A destroying delete of an array, or the one a new-expression records as its free function, is diagnosed.

rows.feature: Class template argument deduction for aggregates and alias templates

rows.note: The front end claims 202207L only.

Evidence in --c++11 GNU mode (the test enables the feature as an extension). The initializer becomes an ordinary member initializer in the front end IL in every mode, so the output does not depend on the mode.
Layout and tail-padding reuse work. Initializing such a member of a class with tail padding with a class value is diagnosed and the function is dropped; so is a constant initialization.
The function that uses it is diagnosed as an unsupported builtin operation and dropped.

A call that takes std::source_location::current() as a default argument passes the address of a source_location object: it is diagnosed ("the address of a non-string constant") and the calling function is dropped.

The cpfe-cir configuration sets COROUTINE_ENABLING_POSSIBLE to 0, and --set_flag=coroutines is rejected under CIR with the command-line error "CIR back end: coroutines are not supported" (M6.1a); --clear_flag stays allowed.
The option --modules is rejected with the command-line error "CIR back end: modules are not supported".
Evidence in --c++11 GNU mode (the test enables the feature as an extension). The IL has no separate form for a static call operator, so the output does not depend on the mode.
Four corpus tests (explicit-obj-constraints, -lambda4, -lambda5, -lambda9) fail in every configuration (front end).

Evidence in --c++20 mode (the test enables the feature as an extension). The front end resolves if consteval to its non-constant branch before the back end sees it, so the output does not depend on the mode.

rows.note: Packs bound by reference (`auto &[...r]`, `const auto &[...r]`) need the front-end fix of GH #525 (finding P-7, security.md §5), cherry-picked onto `cir` before M6.1b; the probe covers them.

Splices of types, members and values, and reflections as template arguments, work (--set_flag=reflection). A variable of a reflection type (std::meta::info) is diagnosed as an unsupported constant and the function is dropped. The std::meta queries (<meta>) were not probed.
